title: Shadow eval-harness integration plan (shadow outputs → scoring → stored results)
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-12 (Olivia)

Purpose
This doc describes how we connect Shadow Traffic outputs (control + shadow responses) to eval-harness so we can compute quality metrics asynchronously, store the scored results with strong rubric/version traceability, and make those results queryable for Console dashboards + regression alerts.

Scope / What this covers
- Job format(s) emitted by the shadow pipeline to request scoring (the “scoring job envelope”).
- Queueing and worker execution model (rate limiting, retries, dedupe, backpressure).
- Rubric bundles + version pinning strategy (including how we handle rubric updates).
- Storage model for scored results (raw rubric outputs + normalized metrics + aggregates), including retention.

Non-goals (v1)
- Customer-provided arbitrary code execution for custom metrics.
- Full offline historical replay beyond short retention windows.
- Cross-rubric comparability guarantees (we will not automatically normalize between rubric versions).

Assumptions / dependencies
- Shadow routing produces events with stable request_fingerprint and identifies control vs shadow variant ids.
- Prompt/response redaction and artifact storage are handled upstream (or as part of the shadow artifact writer) before eval-harness sees content.
- Telemetry/analytics ingestion can attach scored metrics to an experiment/run/time bucket for aggregation.
- Default metric set (PM-1843) includes a mix of heuristics + model-graded rubrics.

High-level architecture
1) Data plane mirrors sampled requests to one or more shadow targets (fail-open).
2) Shadow artifact writer persists minimal artifacts needed for scoring:
   - input (redacted), control output (redacted), shadow output(s) (redacted)
   - references (artifact URIs), metadata (tenant, route, experiment)
3) Scoring scheduler emits ScoreJob(s) to queue(s) for asynchronous scoring.
4) Scoring workers:
   - load artifacts
   - run eval-harness with pinned rubric bundle/version
   - emit structured results + normalized metrics
5) Results storage:
   - row-level results per (request_fingerprint, variant, rubric_version)
   - periodic aggregates per experiment/time window
6) Console/Alerts query aggregates; drilldowns query sampled examples.

Key constraints
- Shadow scoring must never impact user-facing latency (strict async + bounded compute).
- We must be able to pause/slow scoring when queue backlogs (circuit breaker and backpressure).
- PII handling: scoring sees only redacted artifacts; raw prompts are never placed directly on the queue.
- Cardinality safety: do not store high-cardinality dimensions in time-series metrics; keep them in row store with sampling.

---
Job format
We use a single “envelope” format for the queue message, with artifact references rather than embedding prompt/response payloads.

Message name: ShadowScoreJobV1
Encoding: JSON
Queue topic: shadow.score.jobs.v1

Required fields
- job_id: UUID (server-generated)
- idempotency_key: string (see Idempotency/Dedupe)
- tenant_id: string
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- region: string (logical region; for Private, customer-defined region label)
- route_id: string
- experiment_id: string (shadow experiment)
- experiment_run_id: string (a run instance; changes when experiment restarts)
- request_fingerprint: string (stable deterministic hash)
- sampled_at: RFC3339 timestamp
- control_variant_id: string (e.g., model@ver + config hash)
- shadow_variant_id: string
- artifact_bundle_uri: string (pointer to stored artifacts; contains redacted input + outputs)
- rubric_bundle_id: string (e.g., quality-default)
- rubric_bundle_version: string (semver, pinned at experiment start, e.g., 1.0.3)
- scorer_version: string (version of our adapter/runner, e.g., shadow-scorer@0.6.1)

Optional fields
- eval_model_id: string (model used for model-graded scoring; defaults per rubric bundle)
- priority: low | normal | high (high used only for dogfood / oncall debugging)
- segment_tags: string (pre-bucketed tags only; must be low-cardinality, e.g., “endpoint:chat”, “customer_tier:beta”)
- max_cost_tokens: string (soft cap used by worker; “auto” allowed)
- trace_id: string (for distributed tracing across shadow pipeline components)

Example message (illustrative)
{
  "job_id": "6b3f6a5a-5f67-4b35-9c39-7fd4c7ef0b3a",
  "idempotency_key": "expRun=shr_01H..|fp=7f2c..|shadow=var_b|rubric=quality-default@1.0.3",
  "tenant_id": "tnt_aurora_devtools",
  "deployment_mode": "dedicated",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "route_id": "rt_4f9a",
  "experiment_id": "shr_exp_018",
  "experiment_run_id": "shr_run_2026_02_11_a",
  "request_fingerprint": "7f2c9ad0f6b6a1b7...",
  "sampled_at": "2026-02-11T23:18:02Z",
  "control_variant_id": "llama3.1-70b-instruct@2026-01-20|q=fp16|cfg=8d12",
  "shadow_variant_id": "llama3.1-70b-instruct@2026-02-05|q=int8|cfg=91aa",
  "artifact_bundle_uri": "s3://shadow-artifacts/ded/tnt_.../shr_run_.../fp_7f2c...jsonl.gz",
  "rubric_bundle_id": "quality-default",
  "rubric_bundle_version": "1.0.3",
  "scorer_version": "shadow-scorer@0.6.1",
  "priority": "normal",
  "segment_tags": "endpoint:chat,traffic:prod"
}

Artifact bundle contents (by reference)
Artifact bundle is a small JSON/JSONL object stored in our artifact store. It contains only redacted fields.
Minimum fields in bundle:
- input:
  - request_type (chat|completion|tools|embeddings)
  - messages / prompt (redacted)
  - tool definitions (redacted/allowlisted)
  - system metadata (safe allowlist only)
- outputs:
  - control_text (redacted)
  - shadow_text (redacted)
  - finish_reason(s)
  - token_usage (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)
  - safety_filter_outcome if available
- capture_metadata:
  - redaction_profile_id
  - truncation_applied (true/false)
  - capture_error (if partial)

Important: Workers MUST NOT call back into production model endpoints to “re-fetch” outputs. If the artifact bundle is missing/invalid, we mark scoring as failed and rely on retry/repair.

---
Queueing and worker model
We treat scoring as a best-effort async pipeline with explicit SLOs for lag, but not a hard dependency for serving.

Queues
- Primary: shadow.score.jobs.v1 (standard priority)
- Optional: shadow.score.jobs.high.v1 (only internal tenants / debugging; gated)

Scheduling
- The scheduler emits one job per (request_fingerprint, shadow_variant) pair.
- For multi-shadow targets, we emit N jobs (one per shadow variant). Control is included in the artifact bundle to compute deltas.

Worker execution
- Worker pulls job, downloads artifact bundle, runs eval-harness locally.
- Worker emits result to:
  (a) results row store (shadow_scoring_results)
  (b) metrics/aggregation stream (shadow_scoring_metrics_events) for rollup

Concurrency and rate limiting
- Global max in-flight jobs per region (configurable; initial: 2k)
- Per-tenant max in-flight (configurable; initial: 200)
- Per-rubric model-graded eval rate cap (to avoid blowing GPU budget)
- Hard “compute kill switch” that disables model-graded metrics while keeping heuristics (SRE requested)

Retries
- Retryable failures: transient artifact download errors, eval model timeouts, dependency unavailability
- Non-retryable: schema validation errors, missing required fields, rubric bundle not found

Retry policy (initial)
- max_attempts: 6
- backoff: exponential (30s, 2m, 10m, 30m, 2h, 6h)
- max_age: 24h (after which we stop retrying and mark job as expired)

Idempotency / dedupe
We must avoid duplicate scoring when the scheduler re-emits due to pipeline retries.
- idempotency_key format: exp_run + request_fingerprint + shadow_variant_id + rubric_bundle_id@version
- We write results using UPSERT semantics on (tenant_id, experiment_run_id, request_fingerprint, shadow_variant_id, rubric_bundle_id, rubric_bundle_version).
- Worker first checks “already_scored” flag via a cheap lookup (or writes with INSERT…ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING then loads existing).

Backpressure & circuit breakers
- If queue lag > threshold (see SRE guardrails), scheduler reduces emission rate and/or drops low priority jobs.
- If artifact store errors spike, worker trips circuit breaker to stop hot-loop retries and surfaces a single consolidated alarm.
- If eval model provider (internal) is degraded, workers switch to “heuristics-only mode” if rubric bundle supports it.

---
Rubric bundles and versioning
We need stable evaluation definitions so that (a) experiments are reproducible and (b) comparisons are meaningful.

Definitions
- Rubric bundle: named set of metric definitions and prompts/templates, e.g., quality-default, safety-default.
- Rubric bundle version: semver string pinned at experiment creation (e.g., 1.0.3). Patch version changes are allowed without changing meaning; minor/major indicate potential meaning changes.
- Rubric runner version: version of the code executing the rubric (eval-harness + adapter + template compilation).

Pinning rules (v1)
- When a shadow experiment is created, control plane stores rubric_bundle_id + rubric_bundle_version.
- All jobs emitted for that experiment_run must use the pinned version.
- If bundle version is deprecated, job is still scorable as long as templates are available (we keep old versions for at least 90 days).

Compatibility rules
- We do not compute “automatic deltas across rubric versions.”
- Console will show a banner if comparing runs with different rubric versions.

Rubric registry
- Source of truth: eval-harness rubric registry (git tag/releases) mirrored into internal artifact store for Private deployments.
- For Hosted/Dedicated: workers fetch rubric definitions from registry cache (warm in-region).
- For Private: rubrics are packaged with the release; upgrades require customer upgrade.

Rubric bundle contents (expected)
- metric_definitions.yaml (names, types, thresholds, aggregation hints)
- prompts/ (model-graded templates)
- heuristics/ (rules, regexes, JSON schema validators)
- calibration.md (notes; not executed)

Metric naming convention
All metrics emitted should follow: quality.<bundle>.<metric_name>
Examples:
- quality.default.format_adherence.pass_rate
- quality.default.instruction_following.score_avg
- quality.default.safety.refusal_rate

---
Storage model (scored results)
We split storage into (1) a row store for drilldown and (2) rollups for fast charts/alerts.

1) Row-level results table (source of truth)
Table: shadow_scoring_results
Retention: 30 days default (Dedicated configurable; Private configurable; see retention policy doc)

Primary key (logical)
- tenant_id
- experiment_run_id
- request_fingerprint
- shadow_variant_id
- rubric_bundle_id
- rubric_bundle_version

Columns (conceptual; exact schema owned by Telemetry team)
- sampled_at
- region
- route_id
- control_variant_id
- artifact_bundle_uri
- scoring_status: success | failed | expired | partial
- error_code / error_message (truncated)
- scorer_version
- eval_harness_version
- rubric_runner_commit
- metrics_json: normalized metric values (flat map; stored as JSON string)
- rubric_raw_json: raw rubric outputs (string; size-capped; may be omitted for Private if configured)
- debug_notes: string (only for internal tenants; gated)

We will store both normalized metrics (for aggregation) and raw rubric outputs (for debugging and rubric iteration). Raw outputs are size-capped; if overflow, store a pointer (rubric_raw_uri) to blob storage.

2) Example index table (for Console drilldown)
Table: shadow_scoring_examples
Retention: 7 days default for input/output snippets
- Stores small snippets / previews for UI (redacted, truncated)
- Includes pointers to full artifact bundle for deeper debug (RBAC-gated)

3) Aggregates
Table: shadow_quality_aggregates_hourly (or equivalent)
Retention: 90 days
Dimensions (strictly limited)
- tenant_id
- experiment_id
- experiment_run_id
- route_id (may be bucketed or sampled for Hosted)
- region
- control_variant_id
- shadow_variant_id
- rubric_bundle_id
- rubric_bundle_version
- hour_bucket
Values
- sample_size
- metric_sum / metric_count (for averages)
- pass_count (for pass rates)
- refusal_count, etc.
- confidence_interval_low/high for selected metrics (computed downstream; see Sana/Selene methodology)

Cardinality notes
- request_fingerprint NEVER appears in aggregates.
- prompt_id/customer_id are not allowed dimensions.
- For Hosted (multi-tenant high volume), route_id breakdown may be restricted to top-K routes per tenant or a sampled subset.

---
How eval-harness is invoked
Adapter responsibility (ENG-5406)
- Transform artifact bundle into eval-harness “example” format.
- Select rubric bundle/version.
- Execute heuristics + model-graded templates.
- Return normalized metrics + raw rubric outputs + runner metadata.

Eval-harness “example” format (conceptual)
- input_text / messages (already redacted)
- expected_output: empty (for online shadow traffic; no golden labels)
- model_output_control
- model_output_shadow
- metadata: request_type, tool_schema_present, truncation_applied, etc.

Important: For online shadow traffic, many metrics are relative (shadow vs control) and/or rubric-based without gold labels. The adapter should compute:
- Per-variant absolute metrics (e.g., format adherence on shadow output)
- Pairwise deltas where appropriate (e.g., “shadow_has_more_refusals_than_control”)
But we must be careful: aggregation should not double-count. The normalization contract below addresses this.

Normalization contract (output)
We standardize each metric to a simple numeric or boolean form.
- boolean metrics become 0/1
- scores are float in [0,1] where possible; otherwise documented range
- missing metric => omitted (not null) and a “metrics_present” list included

---
Failure modes and how we represent them
We need to distinguish:
- “Shadow inference failed” (shadow target error/timeout) vs “Scoring failed” (eval-harness failure).
- “Partial capture” (streaming cut off) where heuristics may run but model-graded is unsafe.

Status mapping
- If shadow output missing: scoring_status=partial, and only metrics that are defined on available text run.
- If artifact bundle missing/invalid: scoring_status=failed, error_code=ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND|ARTIFACT_SCHEMA_INVALID.
- If eval model unavailable/timeouts: scoring_status=partial (heuristics-only) if allowed; else failed.
- Expired job (older than max_age): scoring_status=expired.

---
Private deployments considerations
- Rubric registry: shipped with release; no runtime external fetch.
- Artifact store: local object store (S3-compatible) or filesystem depending on customer.
- Queues: may use customer-managed queue (Kafka/SQS equivalent). We keep the same envelope, with a thin transport adapter.
- Data residency: all artifacts + results remain in-customer boundary.

---
Rollout + Console integration touchpoints
- Rollout object links to experiment_id/experiment_run_id.
- Console queries aggregates for “quality delta” charts.
- Alerts use aggregates with confidence intervals; we do not page on single-example failures.

Must-have fields for Console
- experiment_id, experiment_run_id
- control_variant_id, shadow_variant_id
- rubric_bundle_id + version
- sample_size per window
- metric values + CI where applicable
- scoring lag (derived from sampled_at vs scored_at)

---
Open questions
1) Do we want a single job that scores (control + shadow) together, or separate jobs per variant?
   - Current recommendation: single job per pair (control+shadow) to support pairwise rubrics and reduce artifact downloads.
2) Where should CI computation live?
   - Recommendation: downstream analytics job that reads normalized per-example metrics; not in worker.
3) How to handle streaming partial artifacts?
   - Recommendation: define “partial_ok” flag per metric in rubric definitions. Default false for model-graded.
4) How much raw rubric output do we store by default for Dedicated?
   - Proposed: store raw output for 7 days; normalized metrics for 30+ days.

---
Implementation plan (milestones)
Phase A (week 1–2): Contract + scaffolding
- Finalize ShadowScoreJobV1 schema + idempotency key rules.
- Align artifact bundle schema with redaction pipeline.
- Add rubric bundle/version fields to experiment config (control plane).

Phase B (week 2–4): Adapter + runner
- Implement shadow → eval-harness adapter (ENG-5406).
- Implement heuristics-only fallback path.
- Emit normalized metrics + raw outputs with runner metadata.

Phase C (week 4–6): Storage + aggregation hooks
- Create/extend shadow_scoring_results and aggregates tables.
- Add ingestion of scoring results into aggregation pipeline.
- Validate cardinality constraints.

Phase D (week 6–8): Dogfood + hardening
- Run internal tenants at low sampling (0.1–0.5%).
- Load tests and backpressure verification (coordinate with SRE).
- Document runbook hooks and kill switches.

Acceptance criteria (v1)
- End-to-end: shadow pair captured → job emitted → scored → stored → appears in aggregate dashboard.
- Reproducibility: every aggregate point is traceable to rubric bundle/version and scorer_version.
- Safety: scoring pipeline failures do not impact serving; circuit breakers work.
- Compliance: queue messages contain no raw prompts; only artifact refs.

Notes to self / next edits
- Pull latest rubric bundle naming from PM-1843 once finalized.
- Confirm with Logan/Nadia the exact table names and whether we use JSON columns vs flattened columns for top metrics.
- Confirm with SRE whether heuristics-only mode is automatic or manual toggle at launch.
